summary: Updates RFC 1229, RFC 1230, RFC 1231, RFC 1232 and RFC 1233 with new codes when MIBs move from experimental to standard assignments. It is now historic.

eli5.summary: When some checklists graduated from tryout to official, they needed new labels. This lists the new labels.

subtitle: A short note moving several interface MIBs from experimental to standard object ID numbers.

tldr.problem: MIBs got arcs in the experimental namespace early and only moved to the standard namespace at Full Standard, forcing vendors to revise implementations for no real technical change.
tldr.mechanism: The memo says arcs should be assigned in the standard MIB namespace at the earliest phase and kept, and it lists new codes for five specific MIBs.
tldr.outcome: RFC 1239 is now Historic. It updated RFC 1229 to RFC 1233, and the memo says to consult each MIB publication for new code assignments in the future.

today: RFC 1239 is Historic. It updated RFC 1229, RFC 1230, RFC 1231, RFC 1232 and RFC 1233, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes it.

sections.title: The Old Practice and Its Problems
sections.content:
MIBs used to be given arcs in the experimental MIB namespace early on and were not given arcs in the standard namespace until they reached Full Standard status. That required vendors to revise implementations when a MIB went from Draft to Full Standard, even though there was probably no substantive technical change.

The memo adds that the practice could cause operational problems at an undesirably late stage and could discourage implementation until the Full Standard stage. The preferable practice is to assign standard arcs at the earliest phase and keep them as the standard progresses.
sections.eli5: Changing a label late forces everyone to redo their work. It is better to use the final label from the start.

sections.title: Which MIBs Are Updated
sections.content: The memo updates five documents with new codes: RFC 1229 (Extensions to the Generic-Interface MIB), RFC 1230 (IEEE 802.4 Token Bus MIB), RFC 1231 (IEEE 802.5 Token Ring MIB), RFC 1232 (DS1 Interface Type) and RFC 1233 (DS3 Interface Type). In the future, readers should consult each MIB publication for new code assignments.
sections.eli5: Five documents get new numbers, and from now on you check each document for its own number.

sections.title: Old and New Codes
sections.content:
The old experimental codes sit under prefix 1.3.6.1.3: 2 for T1-Carrier, 4 for IEEE802.5, 6 for the generic Interface extension, 7 for IEEE802.4 and 15 for DS3.

The new standard codes sit under 1.3.6.1.2.1, where 12 is Generic IF, and under the transmission prefix 1.3.6.1.2.1.10, where 8 is IEEE802.4, 9 is IEEE802.5, 18 is DS1 (T1 Carrier objects) and 30 is DS3. The memo says security issues are not discussed.
sections.eli5: It is a lookup table: each old temporary number is matched with its new permanent one.
